content.thinking:
I'm sketching the composition: a red panda roughly 0.6m long with a 0.5m tail, standing on all fours atop a mossy boulder about 0.35m tall and 0.5m wide, facing +Z with its tail curved in an S-shape behind it and head turned for interest.

Now I'm working out proportions numerically—stone top around 0.32m with legs about 0.12m, so the body center sits near y=0.43. For coloring, I'm planning a countershaded coat: rust-red across the back, dark brown/black on the belly and legs, white facial markings, and a ringed tail, using a fur-edge shader approach.

Writing face paint logic...

For tear marks, I'll drape a rough polyline from near the eye down to the muzzle onto the head surface, then sweep a thin dark brown tube along it to render the tear streak.

Keeping the head facing forward with no joint articulation, I'm now laying out leg geometry: front legs as tapered capsules from shoulder to paw, hind legs with thicker thigh capsules, and flattened sphere paws, plus small spike claws per paw for detail.

For the tail, I'm plotting a catmull-rom curve starting at the hip and arcing back and up in an S-shape, making sure it clears the stone's footprint so it doesn't intersect the surface below.

Still writing tail rings and coloring...

Scattering tuft cards across the body with randomized size, lean, and bend for texture, filtered by surface normal so they favor the upward-facing areas. For the body shape itself, I'm considering a capsule form with tapered radii and wrapping it in the coat paint with fur-edge shading.

I'm adding a haunch sphere and positioning the body axis, plus cheek fluff using small outward-pointing cone tufts around the head. For texture variation, I'm blending moss and stone paints using noise so mossy patches appear more on upward-facing surfaces.

Writing moss clump logic...

I'm also considering tiny glowing flowers on the moss and a cute gold-trimmed collar with a bell, using a thin torus near the neck for the ribbon loop.

Working out the collar torus angle to wrap naturally around the neck, then placing a small gold bell near the chin and a gold ring band at the tail base for that Genshin gold accent touch.

I'm skipping ribbon tassels for simplicity and instead focusing on head details -- cream eyebrow spots, a dark nose sphere, a subtle mouth line, and a cream muzzle sphere, all positioned relative to the head center.

Positioning the muzzle, nose, and eye decals on the head, then painting the head surface rust with cream cheek patches...

Still positioning ear geometry...

Now I'm figuring out the stone surface curvature to determine where the feet should rest, computing the ellipsoid heights at different foot positions so the paws sit naturally on top without floating or sinking too far in.

Hind legs get longer paws, and I'm adding a smaller rock lump near the front side plus checking overall bounds—stone width, tail extension, and total height stay within the model's limits with slight ground sinkage.

For the stone, I'm using a sphere with crack facets drawn via cell noise where close edge distances turn dark, and giving moss a wavy top boundary using layered noise. For the grass tufts, I'm sketching a simple blade shape as an SVG path, tapering from base to tip.

For moss I'll reuse the grass tuft but tint it green, and scatter card clusters across upper stone surfaces using two slightly different green tints for natural variation. The fur-covered body gets an orange tint, and I'm adding small glowing dendro motes as tiny spheres in a yellow-green hue scattered near the stone for an elemental accent.

Still writing stone surface placement logic...

Working out the tail geometry with varying radii and segmented ring bands, then figuring out how to scatter cream tuft cards around the cheeks using normal direction filters since exact position fields aren't accessible.

Adding claws as small spikes at each paw with a directional offset, and sketching in mouth details with thin rods for the smile line under the nose.
